papers.title: An example of a non-sofic hyperbolic group
papers.subject: Group theory
papers.abstract: We construct a torsion-free, two-dimensional, word-hyperbolic group which is not sofic. Our construction builds on OpenAI's construction of a non-residually finite hyperbolic group, see OpenAI 252.
papers.provenance: This paper is based on an AI-generated construction obtained by Harjas Sandhu on October 7, 2026, which was in turn based on the OpenAI breakthrough [14]. The second author worked through the proof to make it readable and to reduce unnecessary overhead.
papers.provenance_summary: The construction inherits marked lines, triangular relations, an interpolation identity and comparisons of real and finite-field ranks from OpenAI 252. The acknowledgments also disclose AI assistance in drafting and explain how the paper relates these ingredients to earlier mathematics. The PDF hosted here is the unchanged arXiv v1 preprint.
papers.summary: A construction of a torsion-free, two-dimensional, word-hyperbolic group that is not sofic, building on OpenAI’s earlier construction of a non-residually finite hyperbolic group.

papers.title: Complete information orders of quantum channels: equivalence and undecidability
papers.contribution: Harjas Sandhu developed and coordinated the agentic system used for these investigations and serves as the manuscript contact, rather than as a scientific author.
papers.subject: Quantum information

companion.description: The companion preprint develops capacity and one-way distillation consequences that depend on the order results presented here.

papers.abstract: With arbitrary finite quantum references, relative entropy, Holevo information and SLD Fisher information induce the same channel order, reversed by complementation. This order is coRE-complete, even for strictly positive rational POVMs. Its bounded entropy defect is additive and uncomputable at every fixed positive additive accuracy.
papers.provenance: The new results and proofs were discovered and developed by AI systems. Harjas Sandhu serves solely as the contact person. Independent specialist review and priority assessment are pending.
papers.summary: A comparison of complete quantum-channel information orders, claiming equivalence of entropy and Fisher-information criteria and undecidability even for strictly positive rational POVMs.

papers.title: From complete channel order to capacity and one-way distillation
papers.contribution: Harjas Sandhu developed and coordinated the agentic system used for these investigations and serves as the manuscript contact, rather than as a scientific author.
papers.subject: Quantum information

companion.description: This manuscript develops capacity and distillation consequences using the complete-order results of the companion preprint.

papers.abstract: A flagged channel with a four-dimensional auxiliary input turns every failed complete information comparison into positive private and quantum capacity. This transfers complete-order undecidability to exact-zero capacity and one-way distillation, even under any prescribed two-way distillation lower bound. All reference transmission and activation use the constructed channel itself.
papers.provenance: The new results and proofs were discovered and developed by AI systems. Harjas Sandhu serves solely as the contact person. Independent specialist review and priority assessment are pending.
papers.summary: A channel construction that claims to turn failed complete information comparisons into positive private and quantum capacity, with consequences for exact-zero capacity and one-way distillation.

selected_research.title: Thermal balance and the amplifier entropy photon-number inequality
selected_research.contribution: Harjas Sandhu developed and coordinated the agentic system used for this investigation. The mathematical development and writing are AI-generated; no human mathematical authorship is assigned.
selected_research.subject: Quantum information and mathematical physics
selected_research.rights_notice: The source bundle retains the Apache License 2.0 and attribution notice for incorporated OpenAI material. See LICENSE and NOTICE.txt for scope.
selected_research.abstract: The entropy photon number is the occupation of a thermal state with a given entropy per mode. We give a variational argument for its sharp lower bound under amplification of two independent finite-energy inputs, allowing correlations within each input group. The proof turns on an agreement of signs: the creation port reverses a logarithmic-mean metric, and thermal relaxation obeys the corresponding signed occupation balance. At a regularized entropy minimum, these two facts cancel the energy corrections and force the thermal-balance defects to vanish. A trace-norm Stein bound, obtained from thermal-attenuator smoothing, then closes the argument. We also give a Gaussian spectral refinement, characterize Gaussian equality by a common symplectic shape, and deduce a sharp correlation bound for the two outputs. The conjecture is due to De Palma, Mari and Giovannetti; the variational framework and four-weight interpolation are adapted from OpenAI's beam-splitter argument.
selected_research.provenance: This manuscript emerged from an iterative, substantially autonomous research process involving several AI systems, with successive rounds of dialogue, mathematical investigation, criticism and rewriting coordinated through human direction. The mathematical development and writing are AI-generated; established contributions are credited in the text.
selected_research.provenance_summary: The variational framework and four-weight interpolation adapt OpenAI’s beam-splitter argument. The amplifier conjecture is credited to De Palma, Mari and Giovannetti. The inherited license and attribution notice are included with the complete source.
